races.title: State Assembly, District 73
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Urson Russell
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 73 (Costa Mesa, Irvine, parts of Tustin). Describes himself as a business owner with 30 years in operations, logistics and manufacturing, and lists chief operating officer as his profession. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements and voter-guide recommendations from Reform California, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, April's Common Sense Cali Voters, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Russell holding public office, so there is no voting or legislative record. We found no stated position or action from him on data centers, property taxes, institutional or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign website gives general principles but no specific policy positions. His survey answers give broad themes such as oversight of taxpayer money, parental involvement in schools, local control, and election administration. His birthplace is described only as Southern California, with no city. We found no independent reporting, such as news coverage, confirming his business history, and no controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: In his Ballotpedia survey he says he is a lifelong Southern Californian, born and raised in SoCal, and Ballotpedia lists Newport Harbor High School as his school; the birthplace claim is self-reported.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Says he has built businesses for 30 years in operations, logistics and manufacturing, co-founded a lithium golf car fleet company, helped launch a wearable camera company, and now makes reusable storage bags; Ballotpedia lists his profession as chief operating officer.
qual.why: He has business ownership and management experience, which falls in the middle band, but no prior legislative or elected service and no documented policy or budget career.
qual.label: He has business ownership and management experience, which falls in the middle band, but no prior legislative or elected service and no documented policy or budget career.

workers-first.evidence: Says in his Ballotpedia survey that he supports secure borders and a merit-based immigration system that protects citizens first, with a legal, vetted path for those who contribute and assimilate. He did not mention H-1B or E-Verify.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: In his Ballotpedia survey he says he is a lifelong Southern Californian, born and raised in SoCal, and Ballotpedia lists Newport Harbor High School as his school; the birthplace claim is self-reported.

cands.name: Cottie Petrie-Norris
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly since 2018, now representing District 73 (Costa Mesa, Irvine, Tustin) and earlier District 74. Yale economics and English graduate with a career in finance, technology and marketing, including Capital One and American Express. Chairs the Utilities and Energy Committee.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.
Her campaign says it is endorsed by local firefighters, teachers, police officers, nurses and small business owners.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace. We found no documented stance from her on data centers or on specific development projects. We found no record of what she did on homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration enforcement or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her sponsored-bill list on Ballotpedia was empty in the page we read, so we could not identify individual bills. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

local.label: Roots 90: Ballotpedia says she grew up in San Diego County and graduated from Helix High School, and her own 2020 survey says the same, but no birthplace appears in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2018, elected in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024. Before that she worked in finance and technology (Capital One business analyst and director, American Express South Africa business manager) and as a marketing consultant and small business owner.
qual.why: Several terms of legislative service plus a finance and business career fit a job of writing law and the state budget. Committee seats and chairmanships, and her Laguna Beach city committee seat, were not counted.
qual.label: Several terms of legislative service plus a finance and business career fit a job of writing law and the state budget. Committee seats and chairmanships, and her Laguna Beach city committee seat, were not counted.

back-police-order.evidence: In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey she said she fights for safe communities and fast emergency response, has the support of local firefighters and law enforcement, and secured state funding for Irvine's Real Time Crime Center, a regional fire and rescue training center, and an Orange County Fire Authority wildfire program.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her 2018 campaign website said that in the Assembly she would fight to protect coastlines, preserve open spaces and ensure clean air and water.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: Ballotpedia says she grew up in San Diego County and graduated from Helix High School, and her own 2020 survey says the same, but no birthplace appears in the pages reviewed.
